run_metadata.coverage_summary: Discovery was performed via WebSearch (extended mode) only. This cloud session's network policy blocks direct page fetches: WebFetch returns getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every non-allowlisted host (all tender portals, buyer sites and aggregators were confirmed unreachable again this run via a test fetch of tenders.gov.au), and the egress proxy only permits package registries, GitHub and Anthropic endpoints. No tender detail page, portal listing or specification document could be opened directly, so ALL findings come from search-engine result summaries and are captured at HEADLINE level only - deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, documents, values and contacts could not be extracted and are left null/empty. Tier 1 was covered across all nine jurisdictions: genuinely current November-December 2026 opportunities were surfaced for Commonwealth (AusTender/DFAT, CSIRO), NSW (buy.nsw - Public Works, NSW RFS, Canterbury-Bankstown, icare, a REZ transaction-advisory RFT), Victoria (Buying for Victoria - Victoria Police, CFA, Ports Victoria, DEECA, Melbourne Water), Queensland (QTenders - Transport and Main Roads reseal/DRFA packages; Bundaberg via VendorPanel), WA (Tenders WA - Water Corporation, North & East Metropolitan Health), SA (DIT via portal/aggregator), Tasmania (LGAT). ACT yielded only aggregator-sourced items with some conflicting dates. NT (QTOL) surfaced nothing confirmable this run. Tier 2 captured council (VendorPanel), water-corporation, health-service and GBE opportunities. Tier 3 (private sector) was queried (SAP Business Network Discovery, SAP Ariba supplier portals, EstimateOne subcontractor packages) but no publicly-visible corporate RFx was found - those channels are registration- or invitation-gated, so only the portals are recorded in discovered_sources and no corporate tenders were invented. Three genuinely new buyer-originated sources were identified (National Library of Australia, Canterbury-Bankstown Council, Insurance and Care NSW/icare).
gaps: WebFetch / direct page fetch is blocked in this session (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for all non-allowlisted hosts; confirmed this run by a test fetch of https://www.tenders.gov.au/atm). No tender detail page, portal search page, or specification document could be opened - so EVERY tender is headline-level only and all are counted in entries_pending_detail. A future run with egress to *.gov.au and buyer domains (or an authenticated portal session) is needed to extract deliverables, requirements, evaluation criteria, documents, values and contacts. To enable, the session's network settings must allow the tender-portal and buyer hosts.

AusTender (tenders.gov.au), NSW buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld.gov.au, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL and ACT Tenders are JavaScript-rendered portals that could not be read directly; Tier 1 coverage relied on search-engine summaries rather than the live portals or their feeds/APIs.
Northern Territory (QTOL, tendersonline.nt.gov.au): no open opportunity with a confirmed November 2026 closing date could be surfaced from search summaries this run; deferred to a future run.

ACT: the official tenders.act.gov.au 'open' listing surfaced mostly long-dated closings (2027-2030). The November 2026 ACT items captured (ICMS Replacement design/discovery, Interpreting & Translating Services) are aggregator-sourced and need confirmation on the official portal. A 'Solar carpark with EV charging' (City & Environment Directorate) item showed conflicting aggregator closing dates (3 Nov vs 19 Nov 2026) and was NOT recorded as a tender to avoid propagating an unverified date.

South Australia: the official tenders.sa.gov.au portal did not appear in search results (searches kept returning South African 'SA' sources). The three SA DIT items are carried from prior runs / aggregator snippets (TenderHub) and still need confirmation on the official SA portal. An SA Health 'Provision of Medical Provider Services' listing appeared current but had no closing date in the summary, so it was not recorded.

Tier 3 private sector: SAP Business Network Discovery, SAP Ariba supplier portals (Woolworths/Coles/BHP/Rio/Fortescue), EstimateOne and major-buyer Coupa/Ariba channels are registration- or invitation-gated; no publicly-visible corporate RFx was found. Invitation-only consultancy/panel RFPs are out of scope and were not fabricated. Capturing corporate opportunities requires authenticated supplier accounts.

Several items (SA DIT packages, QLD TMR reseal packages, WA DFES/WA Police items, some ACT/TAS items) were first spotted via third-party aggregators used only as a discovery signal; they are recorded against the buyer's own government portal, but closing dates/status still need verification on the official portal.

The DFAT development-procurement pipeline page and several aggregator snapshots carried stale 'age' metadata (e.g. '535 days ago') that conflicts with the stated 2026 closing dates; all such closing dates are flagged in notes as needing verification on the buyer's official portal.

WA: aggregator (Australia Tender Alerts) referenced further November items (DFES portable fire pumps 11 Nov, DoT SQL Managed Services 18 Nov, WA Police PRESS CCTV 6 Nov, WA Police HQ facade signage 4 Nov) that could not be confirmed on Tenders WA from search summaries and were not recorded to avoid fabrication.
